entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_STORE_URL
entries.description: The WooCommerce store's home address, https only, e.g. https://shop.example.com (or https://example.com/shop when WordPress lives in a folder). Every request goes here and nowhere else: the connector refuses http, IP addresses, ports, user names in the address and hostnames that resolve to private networks, and never follows a redirect.
howToGet: Open the store in a browser and copy the address it settles on, including https:// and www. if the store uses it, without /wp-admin or /wp-json.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_KEY
entries.description: Consumer key of a WooCommerce REST API key with Read permission. WooCommerce has no way to ask a key's permission without sending a write, so the connector can't check it; it sends GET requests only, and a Read key keeps the store safe even if that ever failed.
howToGet: In WordPress, open WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API and choose Add key.
Describe it as KaratOS, pick an administrator or shop manager as the user, and set Permissions to Read. Never Write or Read/Write.
Generate the key and copy the Consumer key (it starts ck_) straight into the host's secret store. WooCommerce shows it only once.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_CONSUMER_SECRET
entries.description: Consumer secret of the same Read key. Sent only in the Authorization header over https, never in an address.
howToGet: Copy the Consumer secret (it starts cs_) shown with the key straight into the host's secret store. Never paste it into chat or an issue.

entries.name: WOOCOMMERCE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
entries.description: The secret set on the store's webhooks, which signs each delivery (X-WC-Webhook-Signature). Only needed once webhooks are turned on; the scheduled sync works without it.
howToGet: Generated automatically by npm run secrets:setup. Paste it as the Secret of each webhook under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > Webhooks. Letters and digits only: WooCommerce decodes HTML entities in the secret before signing.
